description: I’m a third-year CSE student interested in AI, machine learning, and software development. I bring creativity, problem-solving skills, adaptability, and a willingness to learn. Our team is looking to connect with participants skilled in Python, AI/ML, and web development. We value collaboration, fresh ideas, and dedication, and aim to build an innovative project by combining our strengths and learning from one another.
summary:
COSMORA – Mission Beyond Earth is an immersive 3D astronaut training game created for NASA Space Apps Challenge. Across 15 missions on the Moon, Mars and an imaginative exoplanet, children experience the challenges of life beyond Earth.

Players customise astronauts, explore alien worlds, navigate low gravity, drive rovers and collect, scan and analyse samples. Guided by COSMO, a voice-enabled robot companion, they learn through hands-on missions.

At its heart is a space-settlement challenge. Players build habitats and life-support systems, manage oxygen, power, water and radiation protection, grow food and lead a five-member crew by assigning tasks. Exploration and survival go hand in hand.

Players can also enter Free Exploration, complete a seven-task Training Academy, discover a hidden Star Rush challenge and unlock a Space Station with an Earth Observation Deck and 14 educational exhibits. Daily challenges, achievements, rewards, a Photo Gallery and Discovery Journal encourage further discovery.

Featuring NASA learning resources related to DONKI, OSDR and Artemis, COSMORA turns space concepts into an engaging experience that sparks curiosity, develops problem-solving skills and inspires the next generation to explore beyond Earth.
details:
Project Details – COSMORA: Mission Beyond Earth

Concept and Working Approach

COSMORA was developed around one central question: What would it actually take for humans to survive, work and establish a sustainable presence beyond Earth?

Designed especially for children, COSMORA transforms this question into an interactive 3D astronaut training and learning experience. Instead of presenting space science as a collection of facts, we created an environment where young learners discover concepts through exploration, experimentation and decision-making. Using a third-person astronaut perspective, explorable 3D environments, interactive objects and mission-based objectives, children experience how different systems depend on one another. For example, constructing a habitat is not enough; its life-support equipment must be connected, powered and maintained. Solar panels generate energy, batteries store it for periods without sunlight, oxygen systems support the crew, and greenhouses introduce the challenge of producing food.

This interconnected gameplay is central to the project. Players must collect the right resources, plan construction, manage limited supplies and respond to changing environmental conditions. Crew companions can also be assigned tasks, introducing teamwork and mission coordination.

Technical Development and Tools

We developed COSMORA as a browser-based 3D experience using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js (r128) for rendering the environments, astronaut models, objects, animations and interactive 3D spaces. The interface adapts to different screen sizes and supports keyboard and touch controls.

We also implemented browser-based progress saving through localStorage, generated audio using the Web Audio API, and optional voice narration through the Speech Synthesis API. The project includes interactive scanning, sample analysis, construction, resource management, a greenhouse simulation and camera controls.

NASA's DONKI API is used in an attempted live space-weather data connection, with an archived-data fallback. Educational content draws on NASA resources relating to Artemis, OSDR and space exploration research. We distinguish live, archived and background information rather than presenting every in-game reading as real-time scientific data.

No specialised hardware is required; the experience runs in a web browser.

Creativity and Innovation

Our creative approach was to bring several learning experiences together rather than build another conventional quiz or space-themed arcade game. We combined exploration, astronaut training, survival planning, construction, agriculture, scientific investigation and crew management into one connected experience.

We also designed COSMO as a friendly robotic guide, introduced adjustable difficulty, astronaut customisation, optional assistance, achievements and persistent progress. Beyond the main missions, the Training Academy, Free Exploration, hidden challenge and Space Station provide different ways for children to engage with the experience and continue discovering at their own pace.

Team Effort, Benefits and Intended Impact

One of our biggest challenges was turning an ambitious technical concept into a working experience despite having very limited prior coding experience as a team. We approached the challenge through research, iterative development, feature integration and team collaboration. Responsibilities were organised across technical development, quality assurance, NASA research, scientific documentation, presentation and submission coordination.

We considered the needs of young learners, intuitive controls, engaging visual design, gradual difficulty, scientific accuracy and the balance between entertainment and meaningful learning. We also considered the limitations of simulations and the importance of being transparent about scientific data.

Our intended impact is to make children curious about the real challenges of human space exploration. By encouraging them to plan, experiment, manage resources and understand cause and effect, COSMORA helps develop scientific thinking, problem-solving, environmental awareness and teamwork. More importantly, we hope to make space science feel accessible and exciting, allowing young learners to see themselves not just as players, but as the engineers, researchers and explorers who may shape humanity's future beyond Earth.
